lines.note: Decisive point is the last Hebrew word: under the kaf the print shows a single horizontal stroke (patach), not the two vertical dots of a shewa, and the dot sits inside the tav (dagesh), not the kaf — matching Reading B's יוּכַתּוּ and the parallel forms יֻכַּתּוּ / יְכַתּוּ on the adjacent lines. Everything else (order of items, plene vav in both יוּ- forms, pointing of כָּתַת, "§ 66. 5.") is identical in A and B and matches the print.

lines.note: All three Hebrew words carry qibbuts (three slanting dots) under the yod, not shewa as in Reading A; the third word has shewa under kaf and dagesh in tav (יֻכְתּוּ, the regular Hophal), not hireq under kaf. Reading B matches the print.
